notes: This bundle is app-agnostic and checked in so host applications can map their own contracts onto LewLM without reading implementation files.
Use the schema refs here for stable request and response shapes, and use /v1/openapi.json for the live route index and operation metadata.
Chat and responses support both application/json and multipart/form-data requests; multipart requests send a JSON-encoded payload_json field plus uniquely named file parts.
Chat and responses can optionally accept citation_context source/chunk packages and return machine-readable citations keyed to ingest ids and labels.
Every non-success response carries {"error": {code, message, details}}. The `errors` section lists every code with its fixed HTTP status and whether the identical request may succeed on retry.

field_notes.identity: One base URL. `x-request-id` (optional, caller-chosen) is echoed on every response and is the cancellation handle; `x-lewlm-correlation-id` is echoed and lands in `metadata.correlation_id`; `x-lewlm-application-id: chap` labels metrics and audit and grants nothing.
field_notes.service_vs_engine_vs_model: `GET /v1/health.status` is this service. Engine reachability is `health.engines[].state` and `GET /v1/runtime.startup.engines[]` (cached inventory: advertised | stale | failed | unknown; no probe). A request LewLM finds refused marks its endpoint `stale` (or `failed` if never read) at once, with `inventory_error`; the next successful read restores `advertised`. Model warmth is `runtime.startup.warm_models[]` / `GET /v1/runtime/residencies`. A 200 from health never implies an engine is up or a model is warm.
field_notes.model_picker: `GET /v1/models.capability_availability[]` gives, per model: `chat_ready`, `reason`, `endpoint_id`/`engine_profile`/`execution_locality` (null for packaged runtimes), and `engine_state` (`packaged`, or the endpoint's cached state). When the engine is down, `reason` names the endpoint, its state and error; `fallback_model_id` is set when an explicit fallback alias would answer a chat for the model anyway (`chat_ready` stays false). `GET /v1/models/{id}/capabilities.structured_output` predicts enforcement before a request is spent; `capabilities.tool_calling.support` (`native` | `prompt_guided` | `none`) says whether and how declared tools reach the model, and `parallel` whether one reply can carry several calls (`null`: the engine decides).
field_notes.chat_metadata: `metadata.model` names `resolved_model_id`, `runtime_name`, `endpoint_id`, `engine_profile`, `execution_locality`; `metadata.routing.fallback_from_model_id`/`fallback_reason` are set only when an explicit fallback alias substituted the model before generation; `metadata.serving.runtime_adapter_kind` is `backend_native_batch` for engines that batch themselves.
field_notes.finish_reason: Both surfaces publish why generation stopped from one vocabulary: chat in `choices[0].finish_reason`, responses in `finish_reason` on the sync body and on the terminal chunk (`done: true`). `length` means the reply hit the output limit and is truncated; `stop` means the model finished; `tool_calls` means it stopped to call a tool.
field_notes.usage: `usage` is on the non-streaming body and on the terminal streaming chunk only; earlier chunks carry `usage: null`. `usage.measured` is false when counts were estimated. `usage.cached_tokens` is present only when the backend reported prefix-cache hits; absent means unknown.
field_notes.streaming: SSE `data:` frames of `chat.stream` chunks, then `data: [DONE]`. Exactly one chunk carries a non-null `finish_reason` (`stop`, `length`, `tool_calls`, `cancelled`, or `error`). Native tool-call fragments arrive as `delta.tool_calls[]` with `index` for live rendering; the terminal chunk's `tool_calls` carries LewLM's parsed, schema-validated verdict, exactly as the sync body does, so a client never reassembles fragments.
field_notes.incomplete_stream: If generation fails after output has started, the stream still returns HTTP 200: the last chunk has `finish_reason: "error"` and an `error` envelope (`code`, `message`, redacted `details`, `partial_output: true`), followed by `[DONE]`. Delivered text stands; LewLM never replays. A cancelled stream ends with `finish_reason: "cancelled"`. A stream refused before any output (an unreachable engine) is not opened: it gets the same HTTP error as the sync request.
field_notes.errors: Every non-2xx body is `{"error": {code, message, details}}`; codes and fixed statuses are in `errors`. An unreachable engine behind an explicitly requested model is `503 runtime_unavailable` with `details.endpoint_id`; an unknown model is `404 model_not_found`. Raw backend payloads and credentials are never included.
field_notes.events: `GET /v1/events` (SSE) and the WebSocket carry the same filters (`types`, `scope`, `request_id`, `model_id`, `exclude_types`). Every frame has a cursor (`id:` line; `cursor` in the body). Resume with `Last-Event-ID` or `?after=`: the stream starts with `events.resumed` (`replayed`, `lost` — `null` for a cursor from another server lifetime — `latest`), then the replayed events under their original cursors, then live ones. Retained: `LEWLM_EVENT_REPLAY_BUFFER_SIZE` (4096) events across every type.
field_notes.tool_results: Continue a tool call by sending the assistant turn back with `tool_calls` (`[{id, type: "function", function: {name, arguments}}]`, `id` = the reported `call_id`; `content` may be null) and one `tool` message per result with `tool_call_id`. Engines that take these fields get them; packaged runtimes see the calls rendered in the prompt's tool-call shape. `tool_call_id` is refused on any role but `tool`, and `tool_calls` on any but `assistant`.
field_notes.absent_fields: Optional fields are omitted or null rather than fabricated: `usage.cached_tokens`, `structured_output` (only when a contract was requested), `tool_calls` (only when tools were offered), `prompt_trace` (only with `include_prompt_trace`), `metadata.routing.fallback_*`, `startup.engines[].first_advertised_at` (until first inventory read).

notes: Milestone 120 defines normalized vocabulary and acceptance states only; it does not claim that every term is already implemented on every runtime path.
Support-path labels such as packaged and bridge remain orthogonal to acceptance states such as lewlm_owned, backend_native, partial, fallback, unsupported, and unverified.
Later milestones should reuse these exact vocabulary keys instead of introducing new near-duplicates for runtime, bridge, semantic, document, or agent-surface reporting.
